How to Choose a Hair Transplant Surgeon in NYC: 12 Questions to Ask

Looking for the best hair transplant clinic in NYC? Use these 12 questions to compare surgeons, check licenses and spot red flags before you book.

2026-09-27

There is no single "best hair transplant clinic in NYC" for everyone. The best clinic for you is the one that diagnoses your hair loss properly, plans for your future and is clear about who does what. These 12 questions help you compare New York clinics on the things that actually affect your result.

TL;DR
  • Verify that the physician is licensed in New York State through the NYSED Office of the Professions online search.
  • Ask who performs each surgical step, since some clinics let unlicensed technicians do surgical work.
  • Compare written plans: diagnosis, graft estimate, donor strategy, hairline design, price and aftercare.

Before you book: check the license

In New York, you can look up a physician on the NYSED Office of the Professions online verification search. It shows whether a license is current and whether there are public enforcement actions. This takes two minutes and is worth doing for any clinic you consider.

The International Society of Hair Restoration Surgery (ISHRS) warns about a growing risk of unlicensed technicians performing substantial parts of hair restoration surgery. Asking about roles is not rude; it is part of a responsible decision.

The 12 questions to ask

Diagnosis and candidacy

  1. What is causing my hair loss? A good consultation starts with a diagnosis, not a graft count.
  2. Am I a good candidate, and if not, what else could help? An honest clinic will sometimes recommend waiting, medication or PRP instead of surgery.
  3. How strong is my donor area, and how much will you leave for the future? Donor hair is limited. Ask how the plan protects it.

The surgical plan

  1. How many grafts do you estimate, and why? Ask how the number relates to the area to be covered and to your donor supply.
  2. Which technique do you recommend for me? Ask the clinician to explain the choice between methods such as Sapphire FUE, classic FUE or DHI.
  3. How will you design my hairline? A natural hairline should suit your age and allow for future loss. See our natural hairline guide.
  4. Who performs each step? Ask who makes the incisions, who extracts the grafts and who places them, and get it in writing.

Evidence and results

  1. Can I see before-and-after photos of patients like me? Look for similar hair type, age and degree of loss, photographed in similar lighting.
  2. What do your reviews say about follow-up? Read the most recent Google reviews, especially what patients say months after surgery.

Cost and aftercare

  1. What exactly does the price include? Ask about medications, PRP, follow-up visits and any extra sessions. Our NYC cost guide explains typical price ranges and financing.
  2. What happens after surgery? Ask who you call with a question, how often you are checked, and when you can expect visible growth. Our recovery timeline explains the usual stages.
  3. What if I am not happy with the growth? Ask how the clinic reviews results and what options exist.

Red flags to watch for

Red flagWhy it matters
A graft count quoted from photos alone, with no examThe donor area and the diagnosis need a clinical exam
Pressure to book on the same dayA good decision needs time to compare plans
Guaranteed density or "100% growth"Results vary; nobody can guarantee them
No clear answer on who performs each stepSurgical steps should be done by licensed, trained people
Very low price with no explanationAsk what is left out of the plan
No follow-up planGrowth takes months, and questions come up

Compare at least two written plans

Ask each clinic for a written plan with the diagnosis, graft estimate, technique, hairline design, price and follow-up. Put them side by side. The clearest plan, not the biggest promise, usually points to the right clinic.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best hair transplant clinic in NYC?

There is no single best clinic for everyone. Compare licensed clinics on diagnosis, donor planning, who performs each step, hairline design, price transparency and aftercare.

How do I check if a hair transplant doctor is licensed in New York?

Use the NYSED Office of the Professions online verification search, which shows license status and public enforcement actions.

Should technicians perform parts of a hair transplant?

The ISHRS warns about unlicensed technicians performing substantial parts of surgery. Ask each clinic who performs each step and get the answer in writing.

How many consultations should I have?

Many patients compare at least two written plans before deciding.

Can a clinic tell me my graft count from photos?

Photos can start the conversation, but a reliable plan requires an in-person exam of the donor area and a diagnosis.
